Además del arte, la deformación de domin: Besides art, domain warping is the basis of several serious things. The morphing between two faces is an interpolated displacement field. The corrective lenses of mobile-phone cameras undo the lens's distortion with exactly this operation. Cartographic projection maps are deformations of the sphere's domain. And in medical imaging, deformable registration aligns two scans of the same patient taken months apart by looking for the field $g$ that makes one fit onto the other.

El tema de matrices transformaba la coor: The matrices topic transformed the coordinate with rotations and scalings; this one transforms it with any function at all. It is a [[fn-concepto|composition of functions]], and the displacement that gets added is a [[av-vectorial|vector field]] over the plane: an arrow at each point.
En el tema de [[gfx-matrices|matrices]]: In the [[gfx-matrices|matrices]] topic the idea that throws everybody appeared: to move a figure you do not touch the figure, you touch the coordinate. There we did it with rotations and scalings, which are rigid and predictable transformations. Now we are going to do it with anything at all, and that is where the block gets truly interesting.

Es difícil no ver aquí a Hokusai y a Tur: It is hard not to see Hokusai and Turner here, who painted water knowing that the eye recognises turbulence without needing it to be correct. But the technical genealogy runs through Ken Perlin again: in his 1985 paper he was already proposing using noise to displace the coordinates of a marble texture, and he left written in two lines the technique that thirty years later would still be feeding half the demoscene.
Es un [[av-vectorial|campo vectorial]] a: It is a [[av-vectorial|vector field]] acting on the plane: where it diverges it stretches, where it converges it clumps, where it rotates it makes a swirl.
Esa columna de la izquierda es, en reali: That left-hand column is, in fact, a [[av-vectorial|vector field]]: an arrow at each point of the plane. Warping space is drawing on a plane to which those arrows have been applied, and the same ideas of [[av-vectorial|vector calculus]] — divergence, curl — describe what is going to happen to the image: where the field diverges the image stretches, where it converges it clumps, and where it rotates it makes a swirl.
